headline: BARKLY RARE EARTHS LIFTS RESOURCE 5-FOLD TO 205 MT — Australian NT Project Becomes One of Sector's Largest Undeveloped REE Deposits
snippet: Barkly Rare Earths has released an updated mineral resource estimate that increases its Northern Territory project to 205 million tonnes — a five-fold increase — pushing it into the ranks of the largest undeveloped rare earth deposits outside China. The company says the resource upgrade follows a systematic infill and step-out drilling campaign completed in mid-2026.

headline: HAWK RESOURCES DRILLS 72.7M OF COPPER FROM SURFACE — 26.7m at 1.51% Cu Headlines Final 2026 Hole at Utah's Cactus Project
snippet: Hawk Resources (ASX: HWK) has closed out its 2026 drill program at the Cactus copper-gold project in Utah with a headline result of 72.7 metres at 0.72% copper from surface, including a higher-grade 26.7-metre sub-interval grading 1.51% Cu. The near-surface continuity of the mineralisation strengthens the case for a resource update at the project.

headline: K2 GOLD DRILLS BEST-EVER GRADES AT NEWMONT ZONE — 36.58m at 2.40 g/t Au Including 16.77m at 4.11 g/t in California
snippet: K2 Gold (TSX-V: KTO) reported its strongest-ever drill results from the Newmont Zone in California, with a 36.58-metre intercept averaging 2.40 g/t gold — the highest-grade result returned in any drill campaign at the project to date. The result includes a 16.77-metre core grading 4.11 g/t Au.

headline: LION ONE DRILLS 44.39 G/T GOLD OVER 2.0M IN NEW UNDERGROUND ZONE 500 — High-Grade Hit Near Previous Intercepts at Fiji Mine
snippet: Lion One Metals (TSX-V: LIO) has returned 2.0 metres grading 44.39 g/t gold from the first underground hole targeting the newly defined Zone 500 at its Tuvatu gold mine in Fiji, intersecting strong mineralisation approximately 40 metres from two previously reported high-grade drill results. The result adds another discovery vector to a mine already in underground production.

headline: USA RARE EARTH DROPS 6% AS CHINA EXTENDS MINERAL EXPORT PAUSE — Gallium, Germanium and Antimony Restrictions Hold; New U.S. Tariffs Loom
snippet: China announced on November 24 that it will keep its pause on export restrictions for gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials shipped to the U.S., sending rare earth equities lower — USA Rare Earth fell 6% to $6.31, Critical Metals declined 5% and MP Materials slipped 3%. Analysts caution that the pause does not resolve the underlying supply-chain vulnerability, and the looming threat of new U.S. tariffs adds a second headwind.

headline: COPPER SENDS TWO SIGNALS — LME Down 20% From September Record While China Physical Premiums Hit All-Time High
snippet: LME three-month copper has fallen roughly 20% from its September record near $14,875 per tonne to around $11,867 on November 26, yet physical copper import premiums in China simultaneously hit all-time highs — a split that analysts say reflects AI-bubble deflation and unwinding U.S. tariff trades in futures markets, while actual industrial demand on the ground remains firm.

headline: METALSOURCE MINING INTERCEPTS 416 G/T SILVER EQUIVALENT OVER 3.6M AT SILVER HILL — High-Grade Zone Extends South of Previous Discovery
snippet: Metalsource Mining (CSE: MSM) has intercepted 17.28 metres of broad silver-equivalent mineralisation at Silver Hill, including a high-grade 3.6-metre core averaging 416 g/t silver equivalent — the first hole drilled south of the previously identified high-grade zone. The result suggests the deposit remains open and potentially larger than current outlines indicate.

headline: 'DID WE GET A BOTTOM?' — Analysts Cite Oversold RSI, Silver Relative Strength as Early Gold Recovery Signs Near $3,567
snippet: A November 26 Kitco commentary argues that gold and silver may have delivered the first technical signal that the brutal selling wave is exhausting itself, pointing to a compressed RSI and silver's refusal to make new lows alongside gold. Bullish confirmation is set at gold above $3,617.80 and silver above $41.77, though gold still sits roughly $290 below its 20-day moving average.

headline: URANIUM NEAR $90 — But Cameco Hasn't Followed; Analysts Explain the Paradox
snippet: With uranium spot holding near $89.70 per pound — up 17% year-over-year and close to multi-decade highs — a Yahoo Finance analysis asks why Cameco and its peers have lost ground in recent months. Answers include below-market long-term contracts that lock realized prices well below spot, production costs rising with inflation, and equity investors rotating to yield-bearing assets as the Fed hikes.

headline: CANADA COURTS GLOBAL INVESTORS — Motley Fool Flags 2 TSX Mining Stocks to Buy Before Year-End as Federal Investment Push Accelerates
snippet: A Motley Fool Canada analysis published November 26 argues that Canada's stepped-up pitch to international capital for critical minerals investment has created a valuation opportunity in select TSX-listed producers, naming two stocks that combine low jurisdictional risk with strong balance sheets as near-term beneficiaries of potential capital inflows.

headline: GOLD SLIPS, SILVER GAINS IN THIN HOLIDAY TRADING — Fed Hike Bets and Dollar Strength Cap Both Metals Near Key Support
snippet: Spot gold eased slightly on November 26 while silver edged higher in holiday-thinned trading as persistent Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations and a firm U.S. dollar weighed on bullion. Next resistance for gold sits at $3,630–$3,650, with a sustained recovery targeting $3,800; support is at $3,500 gold futures and $40 silver futures.
